criteria: Multiple cerebral vascular malformations, OR
Cerebral vascular malformation AND family history of cerebral vascular malformation

indications.name: CADASIL
criteria: A confident clinical diagnosis of CADASIL (cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy) including:
Cerebral ischaemic event below age of 50 or >50 if with a family history of dementia/migraine, AND one or more of:
Cognitive impairment with recurrent ischaemic attacks, OR
Subcortical lacunar lesions on MRI scan in white matter
overlapping: R58 Adult onset neurodegenerative disorder test should be used in atypical cases where a broader differential diagnosis is under consideration

indications.name: Monitoring for G(M)CSF escape mutations
criteria: Individuals on G(M)CSF requiring detection of escape mutations

indications.name: Amelogenesis imperfecta
criteria: Significant developmental abnormalities of enamel quality and/or quantity affecting all or nearly all teeth of both dentitions (primary and secondary), AND
Environmental factors excluded

NOTE: Enamel abnormalities affecting unerupted permanent teeth can be detected on dental radiographs meaning that information about both dentitions is available well before eruption of the first permanent tooth
indications.pathway: Following review by dentist expert in developmental dental disorders

indications.name: Hereditary angioedema types I and II
criteria: Recurrent non-urticarial angioedema, usually of gradual onset involving the peripheries, gut or larynx, usually of gradual onset and lasting 1-5 days and presenting without a family history, AND
Abnormal serum C1INH concentration or function

indications.name: Chromosomal mosaicism - microarray
criteria: Hyper- or hypo- pigmentation following Blaschkos lines (Hypomelanosis of Ito), with associated abnormalities such as neurodevelopmental delay, seizures or asymmetry
overlapping: R327 Mosaic skin disorders – deep sequencing test should be used where the mosaicism is likely to be caused by a single gene

indications.name: Primary hyperaldosteronism - KCNJ5
criteria: Primary hyperaldosteronism presenting under the age of 10 years

indications.name: Facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy - extended testing
criteria: Clinical features strongly suggestive of facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD) in whom a DUX4 contraction has been excluded
overlapping: R74 Facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy test should be used where DUX4 contraction has not been excluded
R82 Limb girdle muscular dystrophy and broader tests such as R381 Other rare neuromuscular disorders should be considered where features are atypical
indications.pathway: Following discussion with Neuromuscular consultant and/or testing laboratory

indications.name: DNA to be stored
criteria: To be requested where genetic testing is likely to be required in future, but further information or discussion is needed before a test request is made
indications.pathway: At any time, including where a sample is available e.g. because phlebotomy is being undertaken for other investigations and a future genetic test is likely to be required

tests.target: No target identified at this stage

indications.name: Inherited predisposition to acute myeloid leukaemia (AML)
criteria: Affected individual (proband) where the individual +/- family history meets one of the following criteria. The proband has:
AML/MDS AND a pre-existing disorder of platelet function, OR
AML/MDS AND ≥1 relative (first / second / third degree relative) with AML/ MDS/ unexplained cytopenia / aplastic anaemia

tests.target: Inherited predisposition to acute myeloid leukaemia (AML) (525)

indications.name: MERRF syndrome
criteria: Clinical features suggestive of MERRF syndrome
indications.pathway: At presentation following assessment by a Consultant in Metabolic Medicine, Neurology, Paediatric Neurology or Clinical Genetics

indications.name: NARP syndrome or maternally inherited Leigh syndrome
criteria: Clinical features suggestive of NARP syndrome (neuropathy, ataxia and retinitis pigmentosa) or MILS (maternally inherited Leigh syndrome)
indications.pathway: At presentation following assessment by a Consultant in Metabolic Medicine, Neurology, Paediatric Neurology or Clinical Genetics

indications.name: Mitochondrial DNA maintenance disorder
criteria: Clinical features suggestive of mtDNA maintenance disorder and/or evidence of mtDNA depletion or multiple mtDNA deletions
overlapping: R63 Possible mitochondrial disorder - nuclear genes test should be considered where a broader range of mitochondrial nuclear genes are potentially causative
indications.pathway: At presentation following assessment by a Consultant in Metabolic Medicine, Neurology, Paediatric Neurology or Clinical Genetics, or following evidence of mtDNA depletion or multiple mtDNA deletions

indications.name: Mitochondrial disorder with complex I deficiency
criteria: Clinical features and laboratory features strongly suggestive of mitochondrial complex I deficiency
overlapping: R63 Possible mitochondrial disorder - nuclear genes test should be considered where a broader range of mitochondrial nuclear genes are potentially causative
indications.pathway: Following laboratory or clinical assessment by a mitochondrial highly specialised service

tests.target: Mitochondrial disorder with complex I deficiency (534)

indications.name: Mitochondrial disorder with complex II deficiency
criteria: Clinical features and laboratory features strongly suggestive of mitochondrial complex II deficiency
overlapping: R63 Possible mitochondrial disorder - nuclear genes test should be considered where a broader range of mitochondrial nuclear genes are potentially causative
indications.pathway: Following laboratory or clinical assessment by a mitochondrial highly specialised service

tests.target: Mitochondrial disorder with complex II deficiency (535)

indications.name: Mitochondrial disorder with complex III deficiency
criteria: Clinical features and laboratory features strongly suggestive of mitochondrial complex III deficiency
overlapping: R63 Possible mitochondrial disorder - nuclear genes test should be considered where a broader range of mitochondrial nuclear genes are potentially causative
indications.pathway: Following laboratory or clinical assessment by a mitochondrial highly specialised service

tests.target: Mitochondrial disorder with complex III deficiency (536)

indications.name: Mitochondrial disorder with complex IV deficiency
criteria: Clinical features and laboratory features strongly suggestive of mitochondrial complex IV deficiency
overlapping: R63 Possible mitochondrial disorder - nuclear genes test should be considered where a broader range of mitochondrial nuclear genes are potentially causative
indications.pathway: Following laboratory or clinical assessment by a mitochondrial highly specialised service

tests.target: Mitochondrial disorder with complex IV deficiency (537)

indications.name: Mitochondrial disorder with complex V deficiency
criteria: Clinical features and laboratory features strongly suggestive of mitochondrial complex V deficiency
overlapping: R63 Possible mitochondrial disorder - nuclear genes test should be considered where a broader range of mitochondrial nuclear genes are potentially causative
indications.pathway: Following laboratory or clinical assessment by a mitochondrial highly specialised service

tests.target: Mitochondrial disorder with complex V deficiency (538)

indications.name: Familial rhabdoid tumours
criteria: Living affected individual (proband) where the proband has atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumour (any age)
NOTE: The proband's cancer should have been confirmed

indications.name: Childhood solid tumours
criteria: Any presentation of an invasive solid tumour diagnosed at age ≤ 14, where no other Testing Criteria are met, OR other test did not identify pathogenic variant, AND the patient has NOT been investigated through:
Tumour WGS, OR
Another large germline cancer susceptibility panel, OR
Exome test through GMS or an alternative route

indications.name: Haemogloginopathy trait or carrier testing
criteria: Individuals who are likely to have or carry a clinically significant haemoglobinopathy trait other than sickle cell disease based on initial protein testing or red cell indices
overlapping: R362 Carrier testing for sickle cell disease should be used for individuals likely to carry the common HbS variant

indications.name: Carrier testing for sickle cell disease
criteria: Individuals who are likely to carry sickle cell disease based on initial protein testing
overlapping: R361 Carrier testing for haemoglobinopathies should be used in individuals likely to be carriers of other haemoglobinopathies

indications.name: Inherited predisposition to GIST
indications.change: Panel details updated; New test component
criteria: Testing of affected individual (proband) where the individual +/- family history meets the following criteria:
The proband has GIST (gastrointestinal stromal tumour) somatically wildtype for KIT and PDGFRA:
Diagnosed age before age 50, OR
With ≥1 relative (first / second / third degree relative) with GIST, phaeochromocytoma / paraganglioma
NOTE: The proband's cancer and majority of reported cancers in the family should have been confirmed

indications.name: DICER1-related cancer predisposition
criteria: Testing of affected individual (proband) where the individual +/- family history meets the following criteria:
Pleuropulmonary blastoma (PPB) in childhood, OR

The proband has ovarian sex cord-stromal tumours OR cystic nephroma, AND a first / second / third degree relative with any solid tumour of childhood or adolescence (age <30) or thyroid gland neoplasia (age <30) [Thyroid gland neoplasia includes multinodular goiter [MNG], adenomas, or differentiated thyroid cancer]
NOTE: The proband's cancer and majority of reported cancers in the family should have been confirmed

indications.name: Fumarate hydratase-related tumour syndromes
criteria: Testing of affected individual (proband) with hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell cancer (HLRCC) or other FH deficiency disorder where the individual +/- family history meets one of the following criteria.
The proband has:
a.
Type 2 papillary OR tubulo-papillary renal tumour at any age, OR
b.
Two of: cutaneous leiomyomata, renal tumour (any histology) OR uterine leiomyomata at any age,
OR
c.
Cutaneous leiomyomata AND one first / second / third degree relative with renal tumour, OR
d.
Cutaneous leiomyomata AND two first / second / third degree relatives with cutaneous leiomyomata OR uterine leiomyomata, OR
e.
Uterine leiomyomata with classic histological features (age <40)

Deceased affected individual (proband) where (i) the individual +/- family history meets one of the above criteria, (ii) appropriate tissue is available (tumour or normal), and (iii) no living affected individual is available for genetic testing
NOTE: Cutaneous leiomyomata should be histologically confirmed; uterine leiomyomata and renal tumours should be medically documented

indications.name: Inherited susceptibility to acute lymphoblastoid leukaemia (ALL)
criteria: Testing of affected individual (proband) where the individual +/- family history meets one of the following criteria
The proband has:
Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL), AND
One first / second / third degree relative with AL, OR
Two first / second / third degree relatives with myeloid/lymphoid/platelet disorder
NOTE: All diagnoses must be medically documented

indications.name: Inherited pancreatic cancer
criteria: Testing of affected individual (proband) where the individual +/- family history meets one of the following criteria. The proband has:
Pancreatic cancer age <50, OR
Pancreatic cancer age <60, AND
a.
Breast cancer age <60, melanoma age <60, OR ovarian cancer, OR
b.
One first / second degree relative with pancreatic cancer age <60, OR
c.
Two first / second degree relatives with any of breast cancer age <60, melanoma age <60, OR ovarian cancer

Deceased affected individual (proband) where (i) the individual +/- family history meets one of the above criteria, (ii) appropriate tissue is available (tumour or normal), and (iii) no living affected individual is available for genetic testing
NOTE: The proband's cancer and majority of reported cancers in the family should have been confirmed.
Pancreatic cancer is adenocarcinoma and not neuroendocrine tumour.

indications.name: Hereditary angioedema type III
criteria: Recurrent non-urticarial angioedema, usually of gradual onset involving the peripheries, gut or larynx, usually of gradual onset and lasting 1-5 days and presenting without a family history, AND Normal serum C1INH concentration or function

indications.name: Validation test
criteria: Confirmation using a second technique where required for diagnostic reporting.
Examples of settings in which this indication may be used include
variants where QC metrics indicate that confirmation with a second technique are necessary
variant where the sample has passed outside an accredited pipeline an confirmation of sample identify is required

indications.name: Malignant hyperthermia
criteria: Confident clinical diagnosis of malignant hyperthermia
indications.pathway: Following discussion with national specialist service

indications.name: Newborn screening for sickle cell disease in a transfused baby
criteria: Newborn screening for sickle cell disease in a baby who has already been transfused

indications.name: RNA to be stored
criteria: To be requested where RNA testing is likely to be required in future, but further information or discussion is needed before a test request is made

tests.target: No target identified at this stage

indications.name: Other sample to be stored
criteria: To be requested where testing of other sample types (for example, lymphocyte culture) is likely to be required in future, but further information or discussion is needed before a test request is made
overlapping: R346 DNA to be stored, R373 RNA to be stored and R322 Skin fibroblasts to be cultured and stored should be used instead where relevant

tests.target: No target identified at this stage

indications.name: Family follow-up testing to aid variant interpretation
criteria: Family follow-up testing to aid variant interpretation

indications.name: Segmental or atypical neurofibromatosis type 1 testing
criteria: Clinical features suggestive of segmental or atypical neurofibromatosis type 1 or individuals with classical neurofibromatosis who have tested negative on gDNA analysis requiring cDNA analysis following discussion with highly specialised service
indications.pathway: Following consultation with highly specialised service

indications.name: Intellectual disability – microarray only
criteria: Unexplained autism or intellectual disability with clinical features not consistent with fragile X syndrome or where fragile X testing has previously been performed Typical fragile X syndrome manifestations in females: learning difficulty (usually mild, IQ often 80-85, but can be moderate or severe LD) Typical fragile X syndrome manifestations in males: moderate to severe developmental delay / learning difficulty (IQ if measured would be 35-70)
overlapping: R27 Congenital malformation and dysmorphism syndromes – likely monogenic or R89 Ultra-rare and atypical monogenic disorders tests should be used in individuals with congenital malformations, dysmorphism or other complex or syndromic presentations

indications.name: Linkage testing for Duchenne or Becker muscular dystrophy
criteria: Families with a confirmed diagnosis of Duchenne or Becker muscular dystrophy with no detectable mutation in dystrophin who require linkage testing to guide management or advice

indications.name: Niemann Pick disease type C
criteria: Clinical and laboratory features characteristic of Niemann-Pick disease type C
overlapping: It is anticipated that many specific metabolic diagnoses will be made through use of broad genomic testing via the R98 Likely inborn error of metabolism - targeted testing is not possible early in the investigative pathway and in cases with atypical features where a broader differential diagnosis is under consideration

indications.name: Other rare neuromuscular disorders
criteria: Clinical features of rare neuromuscular disorder not covered by more specific indications
overlapping: Targeted tests for specific neuromuscular indications where relevant

indications.name: Hypochondroplasia
criteria: Clinical features strongly suggestive of hypochondroplasia
Overlapping clinical indications:
R309 NIPD for FGFR3-related skeletal dysplasias - mutation testing
R24 Achondroplasia testing may also be indicated if clinically relevant
R52 Short stature – SHOX deficiency
R104 Skeletal dysplasia test should be used where features are atypical and a broader range of genes are likely to be causative

indications.name: Linkage testing for Huntington disease
criteria: Families with a confirmed diagnosis of Huntington disease who require linkage testing to guide management or advice

indications.name: Generalised arterial calcification in infancy
criteria: Generalised arterial calcification with onset in the neonatal period

indications.name: Reanalysis of existing data
criteria: Reanalysis of data which has previously been interpreted and reported is required, due to:
New clinical information or clinical events which would substantially change the relevant genomic target,
OR
Sufficient time has passed since the initial analysis that new gene discovery will have substantially increased the relevant genomic target (national approach to be confirmed), OR
A technical or scientific advance requires reanalysis of a group of tests to detect an important new source of actionable diagnoses (national approach to be confirmed)
indications.pathway: Following discussion with the genomics laboratory to ensure stored data is suitable for reanalysis; the national approach to defining events which should trigger analysis remains to be confirmed

indications.name: Linkage testing for congenital adrenal hyperplasia
criteria: Families with a confirmed diagnosis of 21-hydroxylase congenital adrenal hyperplasia with no detectable mutation in CYP21A2 who require linkage testing to guide management or advice

indications.name: NIPD - pre-pregnancy test work-up
criteria: Testing on parental and other family samples to prepare for NIPD in a planned future pregnancy.
Note: this should only be requested in families who qualify for NIPD under the relevant indication and may require further multi-disciplinary or laboratory discussion before approval
indications.pathway: Prior to the pregnancy in which NIPD is planned

indications.name: Multiple exostoses
criteria: Individuals with multiple exostoses (osteochondromas) where a monogenic cause is likely and a molecular diagnosis will contribute to management or advice
indications.pathway: At presentation or when a molecular diagnosis becomes necessary for management or advice

indications.name: Barth syndrome
criteria: Clear clinical and biochemical diagnosis of Barth syndrome in a male patient:

Some or all of cardiomyopathy, neutropenia, skeletal myopathy, prepubertal growth delay, distinctive facial features, and history of unexplained recurrent miscarriage or stillbirths or sudden death in the family, AND
Positive cardiolipin result (MLCL/CL ratio) where available; (patients may also have raised 3MGA)

indications.name: Schwannomatosis
criteria: Testing of an affected individual (proband) where the individual +/- family history meets one of the following criteria
The proband has:
≥1 schwannoma under age 25
≥ 2 schwannomas at any age
≥1 schwannoma at any age, AND ≥ 1 first / second degree relative with schwannoma
NOTE: schwannoma does not include vestibular shwannomas or cutaneous plaques All individuals must have had a negative test for NF2 mutations in blood DNA

indications.name: Mitochondrial neurogastrointestinal encephalopathy
criteria: Clinical features suggestive of mitochondrial neurogastrointestinal encephalopathy (MNGIE) with elevated thymidine and deoxyuridine levels in blood and/or urine

indications.name: Thiamine metabolism dysfunction syndrome 2
criteria: Clinical features and characteristic brain MRI changes suggestive of thiamine metabolism dysfunction syndrome 2 (also known as Biotin-responsive basal ganglia disease / thiamine responsive encephalopathy)

indications.name: Mitochondrial Complex V deficiency, TMEM70 type
criteria: Infantile/paediatric onset hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, raised lactate and raised 3-methylglutaconic acid

indications.name: Maternally inherited cardiomyopathy
criteria: Maternally inherited hypertrophic cardiomyopathy

indications.name: INTERIM INDICATION for urgent single gene testing
criteria: Patient has clinical features indicating a high likelihood of a specific recognisable disorder, AND

Molecular confirmation of the diagnosis is required urgently, where the turnaround time of the relevant clinical indication is not quick enough to contribute to management (e.g. in the context of pregnancy),
AND
A single gene test can be offered by the laboratory for the condition
overlapping: The specific clinical indication for the relevant disorder should be used where the turnaround time is sufficient to answer the clinical question

tests.scope: Small variants Version Summary TD4 R201.

indications.name: Common aneuploidy testing - prenatal
criteria: Prenatal findings requiring common aneuploidy testing including:
abnormal first trimester combined screening, OR
characteristic findings of a common aneuploidy on ultrasound scan
overlapping: R22 Fetus with a likely chromosomal abnormality, OR
R21 Fetus with a likely genetic cause
tests should be used where additional copy number of sequence analysis is required

indications.name: Premature ovarian insufficiency
criteria: Four consecutive months of unexplained amenorrhoea (primary or secondary), AND
Elevated serum FSH of >30IU/L on two separate occasions at least 6 weeks apart, AND
Age of onset is <30 years, AND
Non-genetic causes have been excluded including presence of thyroid and adrenal auto-antibodies
overlapping: R53 Fragile X syndrome should be used for individuals with suspected fragile X syndrome
R54 Hereditary ataxia with onset in adulthood test should be used in preference in individuals with adult onset ataxia given the broad range of possible causes

indications.name: MCADD - Medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency – full ACADM sequencing
criteria: Likely MCADD identified following neonatal screening or diagnostic metabolic testing requiring testing of the full ACADM gene
Overalpping indications:

R105 MCADD - Medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency – common variant test should be used in the first instance except where the testing laboratory specifically guides otherwise Testing following newborn screening should follow the established sample and testing pathways set out in the newborn screening protocol

indications.name: Testing of unaffected individuals for inherited cancer predisposition syndromes
criteria: Germline testing of unaffected individuals for specific inherited cancer predisposition syndromes where the following criteria are met:
There are no living affected relatives available for testing, AND
Any applicable somatic testing on deceased relatives tumour samples has been performed first, AND
The individual to be tested is deemed to have ≥10% chance of having a mutation (deceased first degree relative with ≥20% chance), AND
This is agreed by specialist cancer genetics MDT
NOTE: All cancers must be confirmed

tests.target: As per appropriate inherited cancer indication
